新增完整视觉链路：

```text
项目 Brief

```

## 大师方法不再只是“风格模仿”

系统会研究大师的：

- 问题解决方法
- 构图逻辑
- 字体处理
- 色彩关系
- 材料选择
- 光影控制
- 叙事方式

### `master-guided-art-direction`

从设计历史、流派和大师方法中提炼原创艺术指导方案。

### `master-method-visual-upgrade`

对现有设计进行大师级方法重构，不只增加装饰，而是重新处理构图、字体、视觉焦点、节奏与细节。

### `reference-to-original-system`

将参考图解构为视觉 DNA，再转化成原创设计系统，防止照搬参考图。

### `visual-quality-refinement`

对现有画面自动执行多轮视觉精修，直到达到评分要求或三轮迭代上限。

- 通用渐变光球
- 所有区域平均用力
- 无意义玻璃质感
- 过度锐化
- 塑料化人物皮肤

- 菜品、手部和产品比例异常
- 假景深
- 无物理依据的发光
- 随机材质堆叠
- “黑金即高级”
- 同圆角、同阴影、同卡片
- 只换配色的模板化设计
- 参考图表面照搬

entries.snippet: Intel has introduced an AI-powered tool named the Computer Graphics Visual Quality Metric (CGVQM) to objectively assess gaming image quality. Available on GitHub as a PyTorch application, CGVQM addresses various visual distortions caused by modern rendering techniques such as DLSS, FSR, frame generation, and neural denoising. Traditional metrics like PSNR fall short in evaluating real-time graphics, prompting Intel's researchers to take a more robust two-step approach. They developed a comprehensive video dataset, the Computer Graphics Visual Quality Dataset (CGVQD), capturing diverse graphical distortions, and trained a 3D convolutional neural network (3D-ResNet-18) to identify and score image quality akin to human perception. Human observers first rated the videos to establish a baseline for training. The CGVQM model, particularly its CGVQM-2 and CGVQM-5 versions, demonstrated top-tier performance on both its own and external datasets, showing strong generalization capabilities. Although improvements like transformer architectures and optical flow data could enhance it further, CGVQM already represents a major advance in evaluating real-time graphics, offering a scalable and accurate tool for developers and researchers.
entries.title: Intel releases new tool to measure gaming image quality - AI tool measures impact of upscalers, frame gen, others; Computer Graphics Video Quality Metric now available on GitHub

entries.snippet: Google's newly introduced design language, material design, debuts in Lollipop, the latest Android version. It presents a bright, user-friendly look for phones and tablets. Beyond aesthetics, material design aims to merge graphic design principles with new interface and input ideas, establishing best practices for interactive design. The design treats UI elements as physical objects in 3D space with specific rules for interaction, such as shadow casting, akin to real materials. This approach offers users a more intuitive experience, simulating tangible, touchable material. Furthermore, material design provides comprehensive guidelines to aid designers in creating clear, non-confusing products. Google envisions this language to be timeless, applicable across its array of products, and adaptable for future technological evolution. Despite challenges in getting external designers to adopt the broader conceptual aspects, Google's published detailed specs and conferences are efforts to facilitate this transition. Material design is also forward-looking, preparing for a future where traditional apps might evolve into more integrated and interactive forms.
entries.title: Google's Quest to Write the Rulebook for Interactive Design

entries.snippet: Dieter Rams, a renowned industrial designer known for his "Less is Better" philosophy, lives in a house he designed in Kronberg, near Frankfurt. His home, which functions as a living museum, contains numerous objects and furnishings designed by Rams himself, stemming from his extensive career at Braun where he worked for 40 years until his retirement in 1997. Rams prefers traditional methods, avoiding computers and drawing by hand. His work follows the Bauhaus tradition of form following function, creating simple, functional, and uncluttered products that have a timeless appeal, such as the modular 606 Universal Shelving System still in use today. Despite his design ethos, Rams’ home includes a vast collection of his creations, hinting at a divergence from his minimalist principles. Rams continues to maintain a workshop where he engages in small-scale projects, reflecting his lifelong passion and dedication to design.
entries.title: Dieter Rams at home, 2004

entries.snippet: The article highlights the inclusion of young, emerging graphic designers in the esteemed collection of the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, showcased in the "How Posters Work" exhibition. This exhibition displayed the works of these new artists alongside those of design icons like Paul Rand and Massimo Vignelli. Curated by Ellen Lupton and Caitlin Condell, the exhibition allowed the museum to "fill in gaps" in their collection by exploring contemporary graphic design techniques and beyond the traditional regions of North America and Europe, expanding to include talent from Australia, South Korea, and Japan. Snatching up ephemeral posters poses a challenge, as noted by Lupton, but the exhibition underscores a commitment to preserving these works, betting on the future prominence of these young designers.
entries.title: 9 Emerging Graphic Designers You Should Know

entries.snippet: Harvard University has digitized and made available online over 32,000 artifacts from its extensive Bauhaus collection, including paintings, drawings, photos, and sculptures. The Bauhaus, a German art school founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, aimed to unite art and design into a cohesive artistic language. The school itself operated until 1933, but its influence continued through its alumni, such as Mies van der Rohe, Josef Albers, and Gropius, who spread its teachings internationally. Harvard's Busch-Reisinger Museum has amassed one of the largest Bauhaus collections thanks to donations from Bauhaus members, and the digital archive allows users to browse the collection by medium and search by keywords or artist names. The archive reinforces the Bauhaus' lasting impact on design and makes its historical artifacts more accessible to the public.
entries.title: You Can Now Browse Harvard's Huge Bauhaus Collection Online

entries.snippet: The Bauhaus-Archiv in Berlin, dedicated to documenting and archiving the Bauhaus movement, has revealed its first corporate identity to better present itself to a new generation of design enthusiasts. Sascha Lobe from the Stuttgart design studio L2M3 created this identity, drawing inspiration from Herbert Bayer's Bauhaus-era geometric sans-serif font, Bayer Universal. The updated typeface, called Bayer Next, retains the simple curves of the original but incorporates more than 555 glyphs, creating a varied and comprehensive branding system. Bayer Next aims to reflect contemporary needs while paying homage to the Bauhaus' minimalist yet nuanced aesthetic. This revamped identity comes as the museum plans to expand due to increasing visitor numbers.
entries.title: A Typeface That Mines the Bauhaus' Rich Design History

entries.snippet: Dan Perri is an acclaimed title designer in Hollywood known for creating iconic opening credits that set the tone for films. Perri's career began at a young age and was influenced by renowned designer Saul Bass. He created memorable title sequences for films like "The Exorcist," "Airplane," "Raising Arizona," and the "Nightmare on Elm Street" series. Perri's work involves careful attention to detail, including colors, type size, shadows, and scale, which collectively make a significant impact on the audience. He relies on experience and instincts to design titles that evoke emotions and refer to the film's story, characters, and setting. Over his 40-year career, Perri has designed over 400 title sequences, establishing himself as a master in his field.
entries.title: Meet the Designer Behind Cinema's Most Iconic Movie Titles

entries.snippet: Designer David Peters has assembled a collection of movie title sequences, highlighting the art form's significance in balancing storytelling, typographic design, and Hollywood egos. His collection features notable examples such as Pablo Ferro's work for "Dr. Strangelove" (1963) and Kyle Cooper's for "Seven" (1995). With writer Ken Coupland and designer Dav Rauch, Peters has organized these pieces into a traveling film festival, which will be showcased in museums across the U.S. (visit www.designfilms.org for the schedule). Peters emphasizes that movie titles are a unique type of design film, akin to a graphical user interface on the Internet, and highlights their dual role in conveying information and providing entertainment.

entries.snippet: The Pritzker Architecture Prize, the most prestigious award in the field, has honored many architects since its inception in 1979. Each laureate's best building showcases their unique impact on architecture, reflecting their style, innovation, and influence. Notable examples include the inaugural winner Philip Johnson's Glass House, famous for its modernist design; Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Bilbao, a deconstructivist landmark; and Zaha Hadid's fluid Heydar Aliyev Centre. Each winner has left an indelible mark on the built environment, from Luis Barragán's vibrant Cuadra San Cristóbal to Shigeru Ban's sustainable Cardboard Cathedral. Their works often blend traditional influences with modern techniques, demonstrating diverse architectural expressions that have shaped contemporary architecture globally.
entries.title: See 46 Buildings That Represent the Very Best Work of Pritzker Prize Winners

entries.snippet: The AD100 2025 Hall of Fame honors 40 of the most distinguished professionals in landscape design, architecture, and decorating. The list features notable figures such as Tadao Ando, Louis Benech, Deborah Berke, Jeffrey Bilhuber, and Robert Couturier, highlighting their influential work and contributions. From cities like Osaka, Paris, New York, and London, these creators push the boundaries of design and architecture, inspiring others in their respective fields. The complete list includes international and well-recognized names like Sir Norman Foster, Frank Gehry, Kengo Kuma, Renzo Piano, and Jean Nouvel, reflecting a diverse range of styles and achievements. This prestigious recognition celebrates their innovative efforts in shaping the built environment and advancing the creative industries. For more details about each professional and their work, you can explore their respective websites.
entries.title: Explore the AD100 2025 Hall of Fame

entries.snippet:
The "AD100 2026" list by *Architectural Digest* honors 100 of the most influential and innovative designers, architects, and landscape artists working today. Featuring celebrated talents from across the globe—including cities like New York, Los Angeles, Milan, Paris, London, and Mexico City—the list highlights both seasoned icons and rising creatives. Each entry sheds light on the honorees' signature styles, notable projects, high-profile clients, and upcoming works, ranging from private residences and luxury resorts to public museums and iconic hotels.

Key trends in this year’s list include sustainability, global collaboration, and a blend of traditional and contemporary aesthetics. Some standout projects featured include designs for prestigious venues such as The Met, Centre Pompidou, and Sotheby’s, as well as homes for high-profile clients including celebrities and industry leaders. The list also reflects an emphasis on layered, personalized spaces and cross-disciplinary ventures, such as new product collections and monographs. This year’s AD100 celebrates the diversity, creativity, and boundary-pushing vision shaping the design and architecture world in 2026.

entries.snippet: Erich Dieckmann, a prominent yet largely forgotten Bauhaus furniture designer, is the focus of a new exhibition at the Saxony-Anhalt Art Foundation in Halle, Germany. Dieckmann is known for his innovative tubular steel and wicker furniture designs that were pioneering in mass production. Born in 1896, Dieckmann studied architecture and painting before mastering carpentry at the Bauhaus in Weimar. He later led the carpentry workshop at the State Building College in Weimar and held a significant position at the Burg Giebichenstein School of Arts and Crafts in Halle. The exhibition, titled "Chairs: Dieckmann! The forgotten Bauhäusler Erich Dieckmann," showcases his original works, including his first chair design, and newly reproduced pieces. Dieckmann's career was cut short by the Nazi regime, and he died in 1944 at age 48. The exhibition opens in Halle and will later travel to the Berlin Kulturforum.
entries.title: A Long-Forgotten Bauhaus Designer Gets His Due

entries.snippet: On Friday, Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum in New York will reopen after a three-year, $91 million renovation of the Carnegie Mansion. The transformation includes not only aesthetic updates but also cutting-edge interactive technologies such as high-definition touchscreen tables and an Immersion Room for experiencing America's largest wallpaper collection in full scale. The museum collaborated with 13 design firms for the redesign, which expanded exhibition space sixfold, improved circulation, and integrated new technology while preserving the character of the 1902 building. The new identity includes a custom typeface from Pentagram. The relaunch features ten exhibitions and installations, with a flexible third-floor exhibition space. Additional features, such as a revitalized garden and a stylus called the Pen for enhanced interaction, will debut in 2015.
entries.title: Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum Reopens

entries.snippet: David Alan Chipperfield, a British architect and urban planner, has been awarded the 2023 Pritzker Architecture Prize, the highest honor in architecture. Chipperfield was recognized for his "architecture of understated but transformative civic presence," with his extensive work encompassing over 100 projects over four decades, including cultural, civic, and academic buildings, urban planning, and residences. Notable projects include the James Simon Gallery and the restoration of the Neues Museum in Berlin. Chipperfield's design approach emphasizes the importance of history, culture, and environment, while avoiding trends. He emphasizes the role of architecture in society, focusing on the needs of both visible and invisible clients. The Pritzker jury highlighted his ability to design buildings that harmonize with their specific contexts. Established in 1979, the Pritzker Prize includes a $100,000 grant and a bronze medallion.
entries.title: Pritzker Prize awarded to British architect Chipperfield

entries.snippet: Chinese architect Liu Jiakun, a master in his country but relatively unknown outside, has been awarded this year's Pritzker Prize, the highest honor in architecture. Liu's work, characterized by a deep respect for local environment and culture, includes significant projects in Sichuan province such as West Village in Chengdu and post-earthquake rebuilding with "rebirth bricks." Born in 1956, Liu pursued architecture by accident, drawn initially to writing and the arts. He only started his architecture practice in 1999 after years of other pursuits. Liu’s approach to architecture emphasizes the use of local materials and skills, creating structures that blend seamlessly with their settings. His projects range from museums and universities to urban plans and public spaces, all characterized by thoughtful, innovative design. Liu’s philosophy is to permeate through a place like water, adapting and enhancing the local environment, a metaphor that guides his subtle yet profound architectural interventions.
entries.title: 'I aspire to be like water': the exquisite buildings of Liu Jiakun, winner of architecture's top prize

entries.snippet: Robert Venturi was awarded the Pritzker Prize in 1991, but his surprise was evident with his reaction: "What about Denise?" Denise Scott Brown, his wife, and architectural partner, had significantly contributed to their firm’s success, most notably with the influential book "Learning from Las Vegas". Despite this joint creativity, Scott Brown was denied acknowledgement. Recently, Harvard's Graduate School of Design students initiated a petition to retroactively recognize Scott Brown’s contributions. The petition, supported by prominent figures, has brought attention to sexism in architecture and questioned the dated notion of the solitary "hero architect". At 81, Scott Brown appreciates the petition but desires an inclusion ceremony reflecting a collective and modest recognition rather than another grandiose award celebration.
entries.title: What About Denise?

entries.snippet: The article "Deceptively Conceptual," published on October 10, 2005, explores the evolution of book cover design and its cultural significance, focusing primarily on American market trends from the 1930s onwards. It discusses how the advent of mass-market paperbacks such as Pocket Books transformed the landscape, eventually leading to the development of more modernist and postmodernist designs influenced by minimalism and abstract art. Designers like Alvin Lustig and Paul Rand introduced creative expressions that blended commercial appeal with high art concepts. The postwar era saw a shift towards eclectic, computer-generated designs that draw heavily on historical images, moving away from hand-drawn covers. The article highlights the dual role of book covers as both advertising tools and aesthetic objects, noting the increasing corporate influence on design decisions. It concludes by suggesting that modern book cover design often achieves visual appeal through a mix of new technologies and nostalgic references, even though it may sometimes lack a clear, substantive point of view.
entries.title: Deceptively Conceptual

entries.snippet: Governor JB Pritzker announced six recipients of the 2025 Order of Lincoln, Illinois' highest honor for professional achievement and public service. The honorees are speed skater Bonnie Blair, writer Sandra Cisneros, architect Jeanne Gang, educator Janice K. Jackson, journalist Carol Marin, and Julieanna L. Richardson, founder of The History Makers. The award recognizes individuals for their significant contributions to humanity or the state. The 61st annual convocation will occur on May 3 at the University of Illinois Krannert Center for the Arts, Urbana-Champaign. The event is free and open to the public, with a ticketed reception and dinner following the ceremony. Blair, the first American woman to win five Winter Olympic gold medals, is involved in various charitable activities, including the Alzheimer's Association. Cisneros has received numerous literary awards, and her novel "The House on Mango Street" is widely read. Gang is renowned for her innovative architectural designs, Jackson for her transformative role in Chicago Public Schools, Marin for her distinguished journalism career, and Richardson for preserving African American oral histories.

entries.snippet: Hamish Bowles recounts his recent vibrant trip to Tokyo, which was initially fashion-oriented but turned into an extensive exploration of the city's culture, art, and nightlife. Invited to model for the men's designer Takeo Kikuchi, Bowles reminisces about his first trip 30 years ago, which included visits to iconic places such as the gardens of the Imperial Palace. On his recent visit, he attended Pierpaolo Piccioli's Valentino Pre-Fall 2019 show and explored diverse Tokyo hotspots like Sahsa Kanetanaka, Tsutaya bookshop, various museums including the Yayoi Kusama Museum, and architectural marvels like the Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Museum. He also delved into Tokyo's gastronomic delights from Michelin-starred restaurants to Kobe beef dinners and engaged with influential local figures including artists, designers, and pop-culture icons. His visit concluded with a tour of the Valentino collection reveal and an exciting night at an after-party at Tokyo's exclusive Peter.
entries.title: Hamish Bowles Makes the Most of His Trip to Tokyo for Valentino Pre-Fall-And Then Some

entries.snippet:
A new exhibition titled *Otl Aicher: The Legacy Archive* is being held at Wiedemann Lampe’s gallery in Hoxton Square, London, as part of the 2025 London Design Festival and the Shoreditch Design Triangle. It celebrates the influential work of German designer Otl Aicher (1922–1991), co-founder of the Ulm School of Design and a major figure in modern graphic design. Aicher is best known for his iconic visual identity for the 1972 Munich Olympics, as well as for pioneering work in poster art, pictograms, typefaces, and branding.

Curated by the brand consultancy Wiedemann Lampe, the exhibition showcases rare and original pieces from Aicher’s archive, including a typeface proposal for the Munich Games and brand guidelines for German broadcaster ZDF. Many works come from a private family collection recently acquired by Wiedemann Lampe, who were appointed custodians of the selection.

Benji Wiedemann, creative director at the studio, emphasizes Aicher’s blend of rationalism and emotional visual appeal. The exhibit offers a rare chance to view and even purchase items, making it a must-see for design enthusiasts. The majority of Aicher’s works remain at the HfG Archiv Ulm in Germany.
entries.title: A new exhibition of Otl Aicher's graphic work delves into the legendary designer's process

entries.snippet: This curated list from Wallpaper* highlights 15 essential graphic design books that traverse the history, depth, and diversity of visual culture. The selection spans genres and eras, from mid-century British modernism and iconic branding by Pentagram to quirky collections like a history of crisp packet design. Titles such as *Alphabet Playground* explore experimental typography, while *1,000 Marks* showcases brand identity evolution. Books like *Graphic Classics* and Jens Müller’s historical survey offer comprehensive visual histories, and *Type Team* demystifies typeface pairing. Notably, Luca Lattuga's work revives forgotten Italian type traditions, and *The Art of Lettering* celebrates handcrafted design. Other standout entries include deeply personal reflections, such as John Morgan’s design muses, and thematic explorations like football crest symbolism and Japanese layout design. Each book embodies the belief that design permeates everyday life, from corporate logos to snack packaging, and offers enthusiasts a rich, eclectic lens on graphic design’s past, present, and future.

entries.snippet: Brigitte Franzen wird ab April 2026 neue Direktorin des Bauhaus-Archivs in Berlin. Sie folgt damit auf Annemarie Jaeggi, die nach fast 23 Jahren in den Ruhestand geht. Derzeit ist Franzen Präsidentin der Hochschule für Gestaltung in Offenbach und war zuvor Leiterin des Senckenberg Naturmuseums in Frankfurt am Main. Sie gilt als Expertin für das Neue Bauen und Architekturausstellungen der 1920er Jahre. Das Bauhaus-Archiv, das derzeit renoviert und erweitert wird, beherbergt die weltweit größte Sammlung zum Bauhaus mit Fotos, Möbeln und Designobjekten. Die Sanierung umfasst einen neuen Gebäudekomplex mit Turm, einem unterirdischen Ausstellungsraum sowie die Restaurierung des ursprünglichen Gebäudes von Bauhaus-Gründer Walter Gropius. Ein Wiedereröffnungstermin steht noch nicht fest; Veranstaltungen finden derzeit an einem Ausweichstandort statt.

entries.snippet: The article, "Cracking Open the Armani Archive," delves into the Armani/Silos museum in Milan, which houses Giorgio Armani's extensive fashion legacy spanning four decades. Key exhibits include the influential Gigolo jacket, handpicked by Richard Gere, which revolutionized menswear by introducing softer, more comfortable tailoring. The museum, originally a granary, was transformed by Armani to share his career's narrative and inspire students. It showcases 600 pieces across four levels, demonstrating Armani's consistent innovation and timeless style. The exhibition highlights the enduring relevance and impact of Armani's work on contemporary fashion, while digital archives offer a comprehensive view of his collections. Additionally, the collision between Armani's past and modern cultural icons, such as Italian rapper Ghali, underscores the timeless appeal of his designs. Through Armani/Silos, Armani's legacy is preserved as a living memory, continuing to influence and inspire new generations.

A new free, open-source web font named ShieldFont has been developed to combat AI data scraping. Created by Brazilian creative studio Seneda & Abrucio and Copenhagen-based type foundry Playtype, ShieldFont is designed to appear normal and legible to humans while manipulating the text's underlying code using OpenType glyph substitution. This method alters selected high-frequency English nouns in the HTML to subtly change the sentence meaning, misleading AI data scrapers without disrupting human readability.

Unlike earlier efforts like Ghost Font—which relies on optical illusions and video files—ShieldFont functions consistently across static content and is more practical for broader web use. In controlled tests, over 55% of shielded passages using ShieldFont altered the factual claim of text, enabling it to bypass AI filters and poison AI datasets. The project also includes a toolkit allowing developers to apply the same protection to other typefaces.

ShieldFont isn’t "anti-AI" but challenges the ethics of scraping public content for AI training without consent, aiming to make unauthorized data harvesting harder and riskier. With implementation tools and a full white paper available, ShieldFont is a collective step toward protecting digital creative work.

entries.snippet:
This article explores how solo entrepreneurs can automate workflows using open-source AI agents, specifically OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. Tailored for one-person businesses, these tools function autonomously to manage repetitive tasks like support triage, content drafting, and invoicing, freeing up time for high-impact activities. 

OpenClaw is noted for its fast setup, broad skills library, and multi-channel integration, making it ideal for immediate productivity. In contrast, Hermes Agent specializes in task refinement through self-learning, improving over time but requiring a longer setup. Some advanced users combine both agents—OpenClaw for planning and Hermes for execution—to optimize automation.

Real-world use cases, like the Felix agent, demonstrate the potential ROI, with one agent generating significant revenue in weeks. The article emphasizes safe implementation, likening access control to onboarding a new hire—gradual and task-specific. Founders are advised to start small, on existing hardware, with limited access, and to scale usage as the agent proves reliable.

Additionally, the article outlines a support ecosystem of accessible tools (Calendly, Wave, HubSpot, etc.) that integrate with agents through APIs. While security remains a concern—highlighted by documented vulnerabilities in OpenClaw—best practices like access segmentation help mitigate risks. The key takeaway: treat AI agents as junior team members and grow their responsibilities through proven trust.
entries.title: How to automate workflows using open-source AI agents

entries.snippet:
OpenClaw Skills are modular extensions that enable the OpenClaw agent to interact with specific tools or services. Each skill is housed in its own folder and includes a SKILL.md file—a human-readable document with a name, description, and instructions for use. These skills allow the AI agent to go beyond basic chat functions, managing tasks such as email triage, web searches, and automation workflows.

Skills can be bundled with OpenClaw, installed globally, or scoped to specific workspaces. The official marketplace, ClawHub, offers over 5,400 community-contributed skills. Users can also create custom skills for tailored workflows. Skills only load if system requirements and dependencies, noted in SKILL.md, are met.

The platform supports agent role separation and customized automation workflows by routing tasks based on skills. Unlike Anthropic Claude's account-based instruction sets, OpenClaw Skills are more like plugins—run locally, control external tool access, and rely on models like Claude or GPT-4o for reasoning.

Security is a key concern, as poorly written or malicious skills can execute harmful actions. Users are advised to treat all third-party skills as untrusted code, check their VirusTotal reports, and prefer sandboxed runs. Caution is essential, particularly due to the immature state of the skills marketplace.
entries.title: What are OpenClaw Skills? A detailed guide

This 2025 TechRadar guide highlights the top 10 free web security scanners, offering tools tailored to businesses and individuals seeking to strengthen cybersecurity without financial cost. A web security scanner scans websites, servers, and software for malware, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations, often via remote or automated analyses.

1. **Nessus** is ideal for beginners, offering robust diagnostics and machine learning, though it can be slower than competitors.
2. **Sucuri SiteCheck** suits users seeking simplicity, offering swift front-end scans with limited depth.
3. **ManageEngine Vulnerability Manager Plus** targets businesses, providing patch management, risk analysis, automation, and support for up to 25 devices for free.
4. **OpenVAS**, an open-source solution for advanced users, offers extensive features and protocol support but requires technical proficiency.
5. **Wireshark**, a powerful packet analyzer, excels in diagnostics and monitoring but has a steep learning curve.
6. **Probely** stands out for ease of use and integration into development pipelines, with a developer-friendly interface and helpful support.
7. **Nmap**, a long-standing open-source scanner, is versatile but has an outdated UI.
8. **Vega**, great for detecting SQL injections and XSS, is fast with minor false positives.
9. **Burp Suite Community Edition** is best for hands-on penetration testing, though its features are limited.
10. **HostedScan Security** serves businesses, offering scheduled scans, real-time alerts, and intuitive dashboards, though the free tier has usage limits.

The article also outlines selection criteria including ease of use, depth of scanning, false-positive rates, and integration capabilities.

Open-source game engine Godot is increasingly overwhelmed by a flood of low-quality, AI-generated pull requests (PRs), raising concerns among its maintainers. Rémi Verschelde, a key maintainer and co-founder of W4 Games, highlighted how the volume of these "AI slop" PRs is both exhausting and demoralizing for the team. Maintainers are spending substantial time evaluating whether code was written or meaningfully understood by human contributors, whether it was tested reliably, and whether errors stem from AI or inexperience. This situation threatens Godot’s long-standing commitment to being open and welcoming to new contributors.

The Godot team is exploring solutions, including AI-based detection tools—ironically having to use AI to counteract issues created by AI—but Verschelde is wary of relying further on AI systems. There’s also discussion of potentially migrating from GitHub to deter AI farming, though this risks alienating genuine contributors. GitHub, owned by Microsoft, recently acknowledged this broader issue and introduced new PR restrictions, but skepticism remains over its commitment to curbing AI-generated code. Verschelde emphasizes that increased funding is crucial to hiring more maintainers to handle the influx and protect the integrity of Godot’s development.
entries.title: Open-source game engine Godot is drowning in 'AI slop' code contributions: 'I don't know how long we can keep it up'

After months of heated debate, the Linux kernel project has adopted a formal policy allowing AI-assisted code contributions under strict guidelines aimed at ensuring transparency and accountability. Developers must now use a new "Assisted-by" tag—rather than the legally binding "Signed-off-by"—for code written with AI help. All responsibility for bugs or legal issues remains with the human submitter. This pragmatic approach, endorsed by Linus Torvalds, emphasizes that AI is merely a tool and that the focus should remain on human accountability rather than policing developers' workflows.

The policy resolves tensions within the open-source world sparked by concerns over AI-generated code’s legal and technical implications, especially due to the opaque training data of large language models. Other major projects like Gentoo and NetBSD reacted earlier by banning AI-generated submissions outright. The Linux community had also faced backlash over undisclosed AI usage, such as in the case of NVIDIA's Sasha Levin, where a non-disclosed AI-written patch created performance issues.

By mandating disclosure and reinforcing responsibility, the kernel aims to curb the influx of low-quality "AI slop" and restore trust in open-source contributions, recognizing that AI will be part of coding's future but needs safeguards.
entries.title: Linux lays down the law on AI-generated code, says yes to Copilot, no to AI slop, and humans take the fall for mistakes - after months of fierce debate, Torvalds and maintainers come to an agreement

entries.snippet:
This article explores the invisible yet vital role of open-source software maintainers, spotlighting Daniel Stenberg, the creator of cURL—a foundational internet tool used billions of times daily. Despite its ubiquity, cURL and other open-source projects are maintained by small, often unpaid teams. As digital infrastructure evolves rapidly, these "load-bearing" maintainers must constantly adapt code to stay compatible with changing environments.

The rise of AI coding assistants has complicated this dynamic. While AI tools make it easier to write code, they also flood projects with low-quality or context-lacking contributions. Maintainers, who already struggle with limited resources and recognition, now face the additional burden of sifting through this “AI slop,” consuming valuable time and energy. This trend undermines community-driven development and the incentive structure that sustains open-source work.

Furthermore, AI is eroding traditional learning ecosystems like Stack Overflow and technical blogs, replacing them with private and less communal interactions. As AI shifts software development toward centralized, paywalled environments, concerns grow about the sustainability of permissionless, creator-moderated ecosystems. Ultimately, the article underscores the undervalued labor of maintenance in tech and the vulnerability of communal digital infrastructure in the AI era.

OpenAI has announced enhanced measures to help users identify AI-generated content, particularly images, by integrating content labeling technologies. The company will now apply Google’s SynthID watermarking system alongside C2PA content credentials, creating a dual-layered approach to content verification. SynthID offers durability through transformations like screenshots, while C2PA includes rich metadata about content provenance. This combination aims to make AI-generated content more recognizable and resilient against tampering or accidental data loss during uploads.

OpenAI is also launching a public verification portal that allows users to upload images to check for AI-generated metadata or watermarks, initially focusing on content created via ChatGPT, Codex, or their API. While the tools are not foolproof—since metadata can be stripped—the verification system represents a significant step toward improving transparency and combating misinformation. OpenAI has also joined the C2PA Conformance Program to affirm its adherence to technical standards for secure metadata inclusion. The company aims to expand support to other content types and verification systems to enhance detection across various platforms.
entries.title: OpenAI says it's getting serious about AI detection and labeling

entries.snippet: As generative AI imaging tools become increasingly adept and accessible, distinguishing real from fake images, particularly in the context of significant events like the US presidential election, has become a pressing issue. The C2PA authentication standard, supported by companies such as Microsoft, Adobe, Google, and others, provides a technical solution by attaching verifiable metadata to images, indicating their authenticity and any alterations made. However, despite the robustness of this system, broad adoption has been hindered by interoperability issues and the slow integration across devices and platforms. Although some cameras and software, including Adobe's Photoshop and Lightroom, support this standard, most smartphones and many major platforms, like X (formerly Twitter), do not. Meta has begun tagging AI-generated images but does not currently flag authentic images. The challenge extends beyond technology; convincing the public to trust and use these verification methods remains a hurdle amid pervasive misinformation and skepticism.
entries.title: This system can sort real pictures from AI fakes - why aren't platforms using it?

entries.snippet: YouTube has introduced a new label indicating if a video was captured using a real camera with unaltered footage and audio, utilizing the C2PA standard to verify authenticity. This feature, demonstrated by Trupic, the first to upload an authentic video with C2PA Content Credentials, will apply only to content created with devices and tools supporting the required metadata. The label signifies that the video's origin and integrity are verified, even if minor edits are made, as long as they comply with C2PA standards (version 2.1 or higher). Google aims to enhance transparency regarding AI-generated content, building on their previous "altered or synthetic content" label introduced earlier this year.
entries.title: YouTube takes a baby step toward labeling authentic video

entries.snippet:
As the influence of generative AI deepens, Big Tech has publicly committed to combating misinformation and fake content with systems like C2PA (Content Credentials), a metadata-based tool launched in 2021 to authenticate media. Instagram head Adam Mosseri recently raised concerns about AI eroding authenticity and suggested labeling real media. While C2PA — backed by major players like Meta, Google, Microsoft, Adobe, and OpenAI — offers some benefits, its impact remains limited. It requires universal adoption and is often inconsistently applied or difficult for users to access. Metadata can be stripped from media, and companies like LinkedIn, TikTok, and Instagram struggle to label content reliably. Meta has even mislabeled real photos as AI-generated, prompting backlash.

Critics argue that firms are using C2PA more for optics than effectiveness, while simultaneously producing tools that fuel "AI slop." Platforms profit from controversial and AI-generated content, and their incentives run counter to authentic media preservation. Reality Defender’s CEO points out that labeling alone won't stop the spread of disinformation, especially as AI capabilities continue proliferating. Ultimately, while solutions like C2PA exist, they are far from sufficient substitutes for meaningful accountability by companies that continue to profit from synthetic content.
entries.title: Does Big Tech actually care about fighting AI slop?

entries.snippet: One year after the SolarWinds hack, supply chain threats continue to pose significant risks. The attack, attributed to Russia, highlighted the vulnerabilities of widely used software, allowing attackers potential access to up to 18,000 SolarWinds customers. In response, the technology industry and the US government have made substantial investments to improve cybersecurity. Notably, the US government issued an executive order to mandate more rigorous security measures, and initiatives like software bills of materials (SBOMs) have gained traction. However, challenges remain, particularly with open-source software. Despite progress, experts warn that the threat of similar attacks persists. This year, companies like Codecov and Kaseya have also faced supply chain breaches, and ongoing activities by the attackers behind the SolarWinds hack indicate that the threat landscape remains dynamic and dangerous.
entries.title: A Year After the SolarWinds Hack, Supply Chain Threats Still Loom

Canon has introduced its new Authenticity Imaging System, a C2PA-compliant solution aimed at maintaining image integrity in professional newsrooms. Officially launching in May 2026 across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, the system is initially compatible with Canon's EOS R1 and EOS R5 Mark II cameras. In response to the growing concerns over AI-generated and manipulated images, this technology embeds provenance data at the moment an image is captured. This data includes content history, source details, edit history, and timestamps—ensuring a verifiable record throughout the editorial process.

The system leverages the C2PA standard, which was developed by the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, and adds layers of security with public certificates and trusted timestamps. Reuters assisted in early testing, confirming the reliability of provenance data generation. While primarily designed for journalism, Canon plans to expand its use to sectors such as government, healthcare, and scientific research. This innovation positions Canon as a key player in the broader effort to combat visual misinformation and preserve trust in visual media.

---

# 一、先锁死最终关系：OPEN DESIGN 已经与 WORK LAB 完全分库

WORK LAB 最后一次权威决策已经明确推翻之前的“三模块”方案。

旧方案曾经是：

```text
WORK-LAB
├─ Workflow Assistance
├─ Open Design
└─ Observer
```

当时 `20-design/open-design` 被定义为：

> 设计知识与质量引擎，负责大师研究、视觉方法、质量量表、真实案例迭代、生产交付，并包含 MINIGAME 的 UI/视觉/资产设计能力。fileciteturn72file0L12-L20

但 **2026-08-07 最终决策已经覆盖这个架构**：

```text
WORK-LAB
├─ Workflow Assistance
└─ Observer
```

而：

```text
OPEN DESIGN
→ 完全迁移
→ DTALEX66/OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance
→ 独立生命周期
```

最终权威文件明确规定，WORK-LAB 只保留 Workflow Assistance 与严格只读 Observer，Open Design 不再是 WORK-LAB 模块、支撑区或子产品。fileciteturn68file9L450-L474

### 最终所有权

```text
OPEN_DESIGN_OWNERSHIP = TRANSFERRED_AND_CLOSED
WORK_LAB_DESIGN_SCOPE = NONE
```

WORK LAB 后续不得再：

- 拥有 Open Design；
- 同步 Open Design；
- 更新 Open Design；
- 监控 Open Design；
- 在 WORK LAB 里继续开发设计专属功能。fileciteturn70file1L40-L57

**所以我们当前这个对话就是 Open Design 后续唯一设计主线，WORK LAB 里的设计内容只能作为“迁入资产/历史需求”，不能再产生第二套设计系统。**

---

# 二、WORK LAB 对 OPEN DESIGN 最重要的原始定位

WORK LAB 时期其实已经确认了一个非常重要的方向：

> **OPEN DESIGN 第一优先级不是插件数量，而是解决“不好看、没质感、没感觉、AI 味重”。**

而且当时明确：

> **大师资料是核心依据，不能删除或延后；插件扩张可以延后。** fileciteturn72file14L564-L575

这一点和我们当前这个对话最终形成的方向完全一致。

因此当前 Open Design 后续优先级应该保持：

```text
视觉质量
> 设计感觉
> 大师/风格研究
> 真实案例校准
> 商业生产
> 运行闭环
> 插件数量
```

而不是：

```text
不断增加 Skill
不断增加 Prompt
不断增加模板
```

---

# 三、WORK LAB 里实际已经积累的 Open Design 资产

这是一个非常重要的补充。

WORK LAB 最后一次全面审计时已经记录：

```text
大师 Registry            497 条
大师 Method Cards         77 张
Benchmark briefs          12 个
质量 Rubric               19 套
Source Registry           123 条
```

并且当时 Open Design 结构验证已通过。fileciteturn73file0L11-L33

所以：

## 不能把 WORK LAB 的 Open Design 看成“只有概念”

它实际上已经积累了一批资产。

但问题也非常明显：

```text
有数量
≠
已经证明质量有效
```

当时审计明确指出：

- **420 / 497** 大师条目仍是 `research-seed-unverified`；
- **77 / 497** 有方法卡，但仍全部需要补来源；
- 12 个 benchmark 要求人工标定，但没有可证明的人类校准结果。fileciteturn73file1L167-L181

所以 WORK LAB 留给现在项目最重要的不是“497 个大师”这个数字，而是：

> **把这 497 条从人物名单升级成有来源、有方法、有失败条件、有真实案例证明的设计知识。**

---

# 四、WL-600：大师研究的完整要求

这一块必须正式并入我们当前的大师与风格研究系统。

WORK LAB 当时已经定义得很成熟。

## 1. 保留全部 497 条 Registry

不能因为很多未验证就直接删除。

应该：

```text
497 Master/Studio Registry
        ↓
高影响 Anchor 筛选
        ↓
深度研究
        ↓
Authoritative Method Card
```

而不是一次性把 497 人全写成浅资料。

---

# 五、六大大师研究领域

WORK LAB 指定先从用户高频设计领域做深：

```text
01 品牌设计
02 平面 / 编辑设计
03 字体 / Typography
04 空间 / 展陈
05 视觉 / 摄影 / 3D
06 UI / 游戏视觉
```

fileciteturn73file0L93-L103

这个分类应该直接进入我们当前 V3/V4 的 Master Knowledge Engine。

但现在我建议在此基础上继续扩展成：

```text
01 Brand / Identity
02 Graphic / Poster
03 Editorial
04 Typography
05 Advertising / Campaign
06 Packaging
07 Photography
08 Illustration
09 Art Direction
10 UI / Digital Product
11 Interaction
12 Motion
13 Spatial / Exhibition
14 Environmental Graphics
15 Industrial / Product
16 3D / CGI
17 Film / Title / Visual Narrative
18 Fashion / Luxury Visual
19 Cultural / Museum Design
20 Game / HUD / Entertainment
```

WORK LAB 是基础六域；当前项目继续深化到完整设计谱系。

---

# 六、每张大师卡不能再是“人物简介”

WORK LAB 已经规定：

### Authoritative Method Card 至少需要：

- 两条独立来源；
- 至少一条为 Primary / Institutional Source，例如：
  - 博物馆；
  - 档案馆；
  - 奖项机构；
  - 大师本人；
  - 工作室；
  - 正式出版物；
- 至少比较 **3 个项目或 3 个职业阶段**。fileciteturn73file2L274-L279

而且要明确区分：

```text
OBSERVATION
和
INFERENCE
```

不能把 AI 自己的理解写成大师本人观点。

---

# 七、大师研究真正需要记录什么

WORK LAB 要求大师研究不能只记录：

```text
大师是谁
代表作品
什么风格
```

而必须研究：

```text
解决什么设计问题
↓
面对什么商业/文化/技术约束
↓
如何建立构图
↓
如何处理字体
↓
如何控制颜色
↓
如何使用摄影/图像
↓
如何控制材质
↓
如何建立视觉节奏
↓
为什么这个方法成功
↓
什么时候会失败
↓
生产条件是什么
↓
怎样跨媒介迁移
```

还必须保存：

```text
适用问题
失效条件
制作约束
许可边界
引用边界
跨媒介迁移方法
```

fileciteturn73file0L95-L103

这比我们之前简单说“研究大师风格”更严格。

---

# 八、最关键的大师使用原则：最终去姓名化

WORK LAB 当时已经做出了非常正确的决定：

> 最终给 AI 的生成指令必须**去姓名化**。

例如不能变成：

```text
做成 Dieter Rams 风格
做成 Massimo Vignelli 风格
做成 Saul Bass 风格
```

而应变成：

```text
信息结构高度克制
↓
减少非必要视觉元素
↓
使用有限字体等级
↓
建立严格网格
↓
颜色承担语义而非装饰
↓
图形元素具有明确功能
```

即：

```text
MASTER
→ METHOD
→ DESIGN PRINCIPLE
→ ANONYMOUS DIRECTIVE
```

WORK LAB 明确禁止复制：

- 可识别签名风格；
- 商标；
- 具体作品构图。fileciteturn73file2L274-L279

这个规则要作为当前项目的硬门。

---

# 九、WL-610：真实失败案例系统

这一块非常重要，而且应该直接提高到当前 Open Design 的 P0/P1。

WORK LAB 已经把长期设计失败总结得非常准确。

需要建立 Regression Set 的问题包括：

```text
AI 味重
廉价感
没感觉
构图层级差
字体不好
留白不好
错误透视
材质假
灯光假
人物不真实
食物不真实
锐化过度
品牌系统不一致
小游戏 UI 不好看
```

fileciteturn72file9L287-L311

这和我们真实设计对话里不断遇到的问题高度一致。

---

# 十、每个真实案例必须保存完整迭代证据

WORK LAB 定义每个案例至少保留：

```text
Brief
Reference Evidence
Version A
Version B
Changes
Quality Scores
Regression
Production Constraints
Human Conclusion
```

不能只保存“最后一张好看的图”。fileciteturn73file2L281-L290

我建议当前项目进一步升级成：

```text
cases/<case-id>/
├─ 00-brief/
├─ 01-reference/
├─ 02-failure-baseline/
├─ 03-diagnosis/
├─ 04-direction-a/
├─ 04-direction-b/
├─ 04-direction-c/
├─ 05-selected-direction/
├─ 06-refinement-r1/
├─ 06-refinement-r2/
├─ 07-final/
├─ 08-preflight/
├─ 09-human-evaluation/
└─ CASE_MANIFEST.json
```

---

# 十一、自动评分不能取代人的审美

WORK LAB 明确规定：

> **自动评分只能做筛选和一致性检查，不能替代用户审美标定。**

同时要求建立：

```text
Blind Review
+
Pairwise Comparison
```

也就是不要求用户每次写长篇评价，只需做类似：

```text
A 更好
B 更好
两者都不好
```

逐渐学习真正的视觉偏好。fileciteturn73file2L281-L290

这个原则应该正式进入我们现在的：

```text
Visual Quality Jury
Human Calibration Layer
```

---

# 十二、12 个 Benchmark 不能继续停留在 Brief

WORK LAB 已有：

```text
12 benchmark briefs
```

但审计发现：

```text
没有完整 Human Calibration
```

所以不能宣称质量已经解决。fileciteturn73file1L171-L177

当前应该升级成：

```text
Benchmark Brief
→ Baseline generation
→ V3/V4 generation
→ Blind A/B
→ Human preference
→ Error taxonomy
→ Regression replay
```

最终真正测：

- 第一眼选择率；
- 商业感；
- 高级感；
- 真实感；
- 品牌一致性；
- 设计差异化；
- 可生产性；
- AI 味；
- 返工轮次。

---

# 十三、WL-620：Open Design 真运行闭环

WORK LAB 对 Open Design 与 Workflow 的接口也已经定义了。

旧设计是：

```text
Workflow
    ↓
structured design brief
method-card digest
quality gates
output path
    ↓
Open Design
    ↓
真实生成
```

每轮 Open Design 必须输出：

```text
critique
quality report
comparison
artifact digest
handoff
```

fileciteturn70file2L72-L83

这实际上就是我们当前项目应该继续遵守的 artifact contract。

---

# 十四、必须严格区分“文件存在”和“能力真的工作”

WORK LAB 当时特别强调：

只有：

```text
真实 runtime
+
真实 readback
+
真实 artifact
```

存在时，才能说：

```text
E3 / LIVE INTEGRATION
```

否则只能：

```text
ISOLATED
BLOCKED
UNVERIFIED
```

fileciteturn70file2L72-L77

这和我们当前 V3 的 L1～L5 成熟度非常一致：

```text
L1 文件存在
L2 静态验证
L3 真运行
L4 真项目 + 独立评审
L5 客户 / 生产验收
```

当前 V3 也已经明确：重点领域要进入 Marketplace 至少达到 L4；宣称商业证明必须 L5。fileciteturn72file15L591-L624

---

# 十五、一个非常重要的旧决策：不要先扩插件

WORK LAB 当时已经明确：

> **插件扩展延后到真实质量回归和人类标定通过之后。** fileciteturn72file9L300-L305

因此当前路线应调整为：

### 错误顺序

```text
100 个 Skill
→ 100 个 Plugin
→ 1000 个模板
→ 再看看设计好不好
```

### 正确顺序

```text
真实失败案例
→ 大师方法
→ 风格研究
→ 视觉评分
→ Human Calibration
→ Regression
→ 确认真有提升
→ 再封装 Skill / Plugin
```

---

# 十六、WL-630：MINIGAME 设计域

WORK LAB 对 MINIGAME 的边界也已经非常明确。

需要保留到 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 的只有设计能力：

```text
HUD
移动控制
交互反馈
图标
视觉资产
场景氛围
可读性
尺寸
性能设计约束
设计交付规范
```

fileciteturn70file3L105-L109

可以把旧 runtime：

```text
截图
UI
视觉资产
运行样板
```

作为：

```text
fixture
benchmark
reference
```

但 Open Design 不负责：

```text
Android 工程
微信小游戏平台工程
IAA 变现
上架
后端
游戏运行时维护
```

所以当前项目里的 `minigame-runtime/` 应继续逐渐降级为：

> **设计验证 Fixture，而不是产品 Runtime。**

---

# 十七、WORK LAB → OPEN DESIGN 的正式迁移映射

最终权威包已经规定逐文件迁移映射：

| WORK LAB | OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance |
|---|---|
| `20-design/open-design/opendesign-assistance/` | `opendesign-assistance/` |
| `20-design/open-design/design-system/` | `design-system/` |
| `20-design/open-design/minigame-runtime/` | `minigame-runtime/` |
| `20-design/open-design/project-memory/` | `project-memory/` |
| Open Design 根级规则、许可、README | 根目录或 `project-memory/` |
| 设计专属资料、Source Registry、测试 | 对应目标目录 |

fileciteturn69file1L40-L60

---

# 十八、迁移不能整仓覆盖

每个文件必须分类为：

```text
IDENTICAL
TARGET_NEWER
SOURCE_NEWER
SOURCE_ONLY
TARGET_ONLY
SEMANTIC_CONFLICT
GENERATED_EXCLUDE
SENSITIVE_EXCLUDE
LICENSE_BLOCKED
```

fileciteturn70file4L134-L164

处理原则：

```text
IDENTICAL
→ 不复制

TARGET_NEWER
→ 保留 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance

SOURCE_NEWER
→ 迁移

SOURCE_ONLY
→ 迁移候选

TARGET_ONLY
→ 绝不删除

SEMANTIC_CONFLICT
→ 人工语义合并
```

所以我们当前 V3 的内容优先级高于 WORK LAB 旧副本。

**WORK LAB 是历史来源，不是覆盖目标。**

---

# 十九、迁移必须保留的 Open Design 内容

WORK LAB 最终切割任务特别要求：

**不能在 WORK LAB 里留下：**

- 大师资料；
- 设计知识；
- Open Design 专属插件；
- 设计 Rubric；
- 设计 Source Registry；
- 设计 Adapter；
- 设计 Dashboard；
- 设计 CI；
- 设计事件；
- 设计专属页面。

而且点名包括一些设计来源：

```text
GSAP
GPT Image
OpenMAIC
ITOM
shapeof.world
...
```

这些应该归 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance，而不是 WORK LAB。fileciteturn70file0L10-L28

这也意味着：

> 我们当前全网吸收 Source Registry 还需要专门和 WORK LAB 的旧 123 条来源做一次 Source-by-Source merge。

---

# 二十、明确不能从 WORK LAB 拉入 OPEN DESIGN 的东西

这一点同样重要。

迁移任务明确禁止把 WORK LAB 的控制面复制进设计仓：

```text
WORK LAB Task Ledger
Observer
CI watcher
通用模型路由
Workflow 控制面
全局规则治理
通用 GitHub 编排
Token Monitor
通用任务监控
```

fileciteturn69file2L70-L84

所以当前两个仓的职责应该是：

### WORK-LAB

```text
Task
Rules
Skills governance
Models
Token
CI
Memory governance
Evidence
Observer
Cross-project Workflow
```

### OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance

```text
Design Knowledge
Design Domain Packs
Master Methods
Style Intelligence
Reference DNA
Visual Quality
Rubrics
Human Calibration
Production Preflight
Commercial Handoff
Open Design Plugin Content
Design Benchmark
```

这和我们当前 V3 任务包里的职责定义已经一致。fileciteturn72file13L454-L495

---

# 二十一、WORK LAB 对设计质量留下的真正核心思想

把所有旧内容压缩后，其实只有六件真正重要的事。

## 1. 设计质量优先于插件数量

```text
不好看
没感觉
AI味
```

必须先解决。

## 2. 大师资料不能只是名单

必须：

```text
人物
→ 项目
→ 证据
→ 方法
→ 适用条件
→ 失效条件
→ 匿名设计指令
```

## 3. 风格必须靠案例和方法证明

不能：

```text
Swiss Style = 黑白 + 网格
Luxury = 黑金
Tech = 蓝色光效
Chinese = 红金
```

这种低维标签化必须彻底淘汰。

## 4. 真案例比文档数量重要

```text
A/B
Regression
Human Review
```

才是真证据。

## 5. 自动评分不能取代人的“感觉”

最终视觉判断必须有人类校准。

## 6. 商业设计必须闭环到生产和交付

不是：

```text
出一张图 = 完成
```

而是：

```text
设计
→ 精修
→ 多媒介
→ Preflight
→ Editable
→ Handoff
→ Real Acceptance
```

---

# 二十二、和当前这个对话的 V2 / V2.1 / V3 合并以后

现在可以把历史关系看成：

```text
WORK LAB Open Design
        │
        │ 历史设计资产 + WL-600~630
        ▼
OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 原仓
        │
        ├─ V2 全网吸收
        ├─ V2.1 视觉质感/大师方法增强
        └─ V3 Complete TaskPack
```

当前 **V3 不需要推翻**。

但是 WORK LAB 内容带来了几个必须补强的 Delta。

---

# 二十三、需要正式加入当前 V3 的 WORK LAB Delta

### OD-WL-001｜旧资产 Manifest 对账

对：

observation / inference separation
rights boundary

production conditions
cross-media migration

---

### OD-WL-003｜真实设计失败 Benchmark

必须正式吸收以下失败标签：

```text
AI_FEEL
CHEAP_FEEL
NO_DESIGN_FEEL

TYPOGRAPHY_WEAK

```

并继续扩展。

---

### OD-WL-004｜Blind Pairwise Human Calibration

加入：

```text
A
B

```

的快速人类标定。

最终形成：

```text
Human Preference Dataset
```

---

### OD-WL-005｜12 个历史 Benchmark 实体化

不是保留 Brief。

而是把 12 个全部跑成：

```text
Baseline
→ V3
→ Visual V3

```

---

### OD-WL-006｜Open Design Runtime Evidence

每个真实运行保存：

```text
design brief

quality gate
artifact
critique
comparison

```

---

### OD-WL-007｜MINIGAME Design Domain Pack

正式归入：

```text

```

但 runtime 仅 fixture。

---

### OD-WL-008｜WORK LAB Source Registry 合并

旧 123 条来源与当前 V2 的 112 条、V2.1 大师/风格来源统一做：

```text
Source Identity
License
Authority
Domain
Status
Duplicate
Supersedes
Absorption Method
Evidence Level
```

不能简单相加成“235 条”。

---

# 二十四、最终统一结论

现在关于 **WORK LAB → OPEN DESIGN** 的历史可以彻底收口：

> **WORK LAB 曾经孵化过 Open Design 的设计知识与质量引擎，积累了 497 条大师 Registry、77 张方法卡、12 个 Benchmark、19 套 Rubric 和 123 条来源，同时明确了大师证据化、真实失败案例、人类 A/B 标定、运行时证据、MINIGAME 设计域和生产交付等核心原则。**

但最后决定已经是：

> **所有设计专属内容完全迁移到 `DTALEX66/OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance`；WORK LAB 不再拥有设计域。** fileciteturn70file4L166-L209

而当前 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 的主目标继续保持：

> **让 Open Design 和兼容 Agent 从“会生成设计”升级为“具备专业判断、设计感觉、视觉质感、大师方法、风格理解、真实商业生产和交付能力的 AI 设计团队”。** fileciteturn72file15L591-L605

**从现在开始，我会把上面这些 WORK LAB 的 Open Design 内容作为当前项目的正式历史输入继续使用，不再按 WORK LAB 模块处理。** memcite

# 二、项目正确定位

当前文档反复强调：

- Open Design 是实际设计入口；
- 本仓库不是工作流中心；
- 本仓库只提供提示词、模板、参考实现和增强资料。fileciteturn5file0L2-L2 fileciteturn33file0L2-L2

这个定义在项目早期是正确的，它防止项目重新造一个 Open Design。

但现在这个边界收得过窄。

## 建议升级后的正式定位

> **DTALEX66 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 是一个 Open Design-first、Agent-compatible 的商业设计智能与生产交付增强层。**
>
> 它为 AI 提供设计理解、项目策略、创意方向、视觉语言、专业设计规则、质量评审、生产检查、交付标准和案例学习能力，使 AI 从“生成一张看起来不错的图”，升级为“完成可修改、可复用、可生产、可交付的商业设计项目”。

### 三方职责应重新划分

| 层级 | 负责内容 |
|---|---|
| Open Design | 画布、项目、模型调用、运行时、预览、导出和交互界面 |
| AI Agent / 模型 | 推理、生成、修改、文件操作、图像和代码生产 |
| OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance | 商业设计方法、专业场景管线、领域知识、质量标准、生产规范、交付协议和学习数据 |

因此，本项目不需要抢 Open Design 的主界面，但必须拥有：

- **设计任务流程定义权**
- **商业设计专业标准**
- **输出质量判定权**
- **交付格式和生产门槛**
- **领域案例与经验记忆**

最准确的一句话是：

> **Open Design 负责让 AI 进行设计；OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 负责让 AI 像专业设计团队一样完成商业设计。**

# 四、最严重的结构性问题

旧定义明确表示本仓库“不负责工作流，只提供增强材料”。

但真正的商业设计增强项目必须定义：

→ 创意方向
→ 设计系统

→ 评审
→ 修改

```text

但它们之间没有明确的数据传递合同。

例如一个品牌项目应该是：

```text

→ 竞品与受众分析
→ 品牌策略
→ 三个视觉方向
→ 方向选择

→ KV
→ 海报

→ 交付检查

现有插件不能保证上一步输出被下一步读取，也没有统一项目状态。

## P0-5：质量评分仍然过于主观

当前 `design-qa-critic` 使用十个通用维度，每项 1–5 分。fileciteturn13file0L2-L2

主要问题是：

1. 不同设计门类使用同一套评分；
2. 没有权重；
3. 没有参考图对比；
4. 没有像素、尺寸、对齐、对比度等自动指标；
5. 没有输出证据；
6. 没有多评审者交叉判断；
7. 没有设计修改前后的回归比较。

品牌设计、海报、UI、展厅和包装不应使用同一评分模型。

例如展厅必须增加：

- 观看距离；
- 人体尺度；
- 施工可行性；
- 材料维护；
- 消防和安全；
- 内容密度；
- 现场光照。

品牌必须增加：

- 可识别性；
- 差异化；
- 黑白适配；
- 小尺寸适配；
- 跨媒介稳定性；
- 商标和近似风险。

# 六、缺失的商业生产层

商业项目能否交付，不能只看设计是否好看。

项目至少还缺少以下五类检查器。

## 1. Asset Preflight

检查：

- Logo 是否为正确版本；
- 图片是否达到分辨率要求；
- 字体是否允许商业使用；
- 素材是否存在版权来源；
- 产品比例是否被改变；
- 参考图是否被直接复制。

## 2. Print Preflight

检查：

- RGB / CMYK；
- 出血；
- 安全边距；
- 分辨率；
- 黑色叠印；
- 专色；
- 刀版；
- 字体转曲；
- 印刷尺寸。

## 3. Digital Preflight

检查：

- 屏幕尺寸；
- 移动端适配；
- 对比度；
- 点击区域；
- 图片体积；
- 字体加载；
- 浏览器和设备兼容性。

## 4. Spatial Preflight

检查：

- 真实尺寸；
- 墙面比例；
- 观看距离；
- 人体尺度；
- 材料厚度；
- 安装方式；
- 电源与灯光；
- 施工接缝；
- 内容更新方式。

## 5. Delivery Preflight

检查：

- 是否存在可编辑源文件；
- 是否存在预览文件；
- 是否有字体和素材清单；
- 是否有版本号；
- 是否有颜色、尺寸和生产说明；
- 是否能由另一个设计师继续修改。

```

这才是能够证明“商业化设计增强”的最小完整系统。

---

# 十、分阶段改造优先级

## P0：兼容和真实运行

1. 重写项目定位文件。
2. 将七个旧插件升级到当前 Open Design Manifest。
3. 重写插件脚手架。
4. 新增 `compat.agentSkills`、`od.mode`、`od.context`、pipeline 和 provenance。
5. 建立 `commercial-design-router` 场景。
6. 真实启动 Open Design daemon 验证安装、加载、触发和产物。
7. 增加 Windows CI 与插件 doctor。

## P1：设计智能

1. 建立统一 Brief Schema。
2. 建立参考图分析协议。
3. 建立品牌和竞品分析模块。
4. 把 Markdown 模板转成机器可读 Schema。
5. 建立不同领域的独立评分标准。
6. 引入多评审者 Critique Jury。
7. 支持修改前后差异评估。

## P2：商业生产

1. 建立数字、印刷、空间和资产 Preflight。
2. 建立统一交付 Manifest。
3. 要求所有案例同时输出预览、源文件和交接说明。
4. 建立素材版权和来源记录。
5. 建立版本、审批和客户反馈状态。

## P3：案例和商业化

1. 每个设计门类至少建设三个真实案例。
2. 建立标准 Brief 与基准结果数据集。
3. 建立人工设计师评分记录。
4. 发布版本化插件包。
5. 建立根级许可证和第三方来源清单。
6. 再考虑进入 Open Design Marketplace 或独立发行。

---

# 十一、达到 8 分以上的验收标准

项目不能以“文件数量”作为成熟度指标，应改为以下结果指标：

| 指标 | 目标 |
|---|---:|
| Open Design 插件真实加载成功率 | ≥ 95% |
| 场景 Pipeline 完整执行率 | ≥ 90% |
| 产物带完整 Manifest 的比例 | 100% |
| 可编辑源文件覆盖率 | ≥ 90% |
| 专业生产检查通过率 | ≥ 95% |
| 每个重点领域真实案例数 | ≥ 5 |
| 人工设计师平均评分 | ≥ 8 / 10 |
| 同一品牌多产物风格一致性 | ≥ 90% |
| 修改后评分相对修改前提升 | 可量化且可回放 |
| 素材来源与版权记录覆盖率 | 100% |

---

# 最终判断

这个项目**值得继续深化，而且方向具有商业价值**。

但它真正的竞争力不应是：

> 比 Open Design 多几个设计 Prompt。

因为 Open Design 自身已经拥有插件体系、设计系统、场景管线、Critique、自动化和交付能力。fileciteturn37file0L2-L2 fileciteturn38file0L2-L2

项目应该形成 Open Design 上游没有重点解决的独特能力：

> **中国商业设计语境 + 真实品牌项目 + 平面印刷 + 产品视觉 + 文化墙与展厅 + 商业生产标准 + 设计质感评测 + 可继续修改的完整交付。**

因此，下一阶段不应继续横向堆模板，而应立即从：

```text
插件资料仓库
```

升级为：

```text
设计知识
+ 商业场景 Pipeline
+ 质量评估系统
+ 生产检查系统
+ 标准交付协议
+ 案例学习闭环
```

**建议下一刀：直接进入 V2.0，先重构定位与 Manifest，再落地第一个 `brand-campaign-360` 商业闭环。**

你这个判断是对的，而且这其实是 **OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 下一阶段最核心的问题**。

前面 V3/V4 解决的是：

> AI 有没有设计知识、流程、规范、评估。

但是距离：

> AI 像一个高级设计师一样“有感觉”

还差很远。

目前最大瓶颈不是缺 Prompt，而是：

```
AI生成能力
        ↓
缺少审美判断
        ↓
缺少构图规划
        ↓
缺少视觉筛选
        ↓
缺少精修循环
        ↓
容易漂移
```

所以商业化阶段必须保留：

```
AI 生成
+
AI 自评
+
AI 多方案比较
+
人工最终审核
```

不能完全自动化。

---

# 一、重新定义下一阶段目标

不是：

> 让 AI 自动设计替代设计师

而是：

> 让 AI 从“图片生成器”升级成“设计助理 + 初级艺术指导”。

最终：

```
设计师
    ↓
AI扩大产能
    ↓
AI提供方案
    ↓
AI筛选优化
    ↓
人类审核决策
```

这个方向更现实。

---

# 二、目前 OPEN-DESIGN-Assistance 缺的核心能力

我认为缺 5 个核心 AI 能力。

---

# 1. AI 审美判断模型（最重要）

现在 AI 最大问题：

生成很多，但是不知道哪个好。

需要：

## Visual Critic Engine

类似：

```
生成10张

       ↓

AI视觉评审

       ↓

淘汰8张

       ↓

继续优化2张
```

评价：

```
高级感
商业感
品牌一致性
视觉冲击
信息层级
原创性
耐看程度
```

---

# 可以吸收的开源项目

## ① ImageReward

非常适合研究。

GitHub：

https://github.com/zai-org/ImageReward


用途：

训练：

```
图片偏好排序
```

适合：

- 哪张更符合人类审美
- 哪张更符合 Prompt

可以作为：

```
Visual Preference Model
```

---

## ② CLIP / OpenCLIP

推荐：

https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip


作用：

图片和文字语义匹配。


例如：

判断：

```
商务高端
```

生成图片是否真的符合。


用于：

```
Prompt
   ↓
Image
   ↓
CLIP Score
```

---

## ③ LAION Aesthetic Predictor

非常重要。

GitHub:

https://github.com/christophschuhmann/improved-aesthetic-predictor


作用：

预测：

```
图片美学分
```

可以作为：

```
Aesthetic Score
```

---

# 2. 构图能力增强

这是你一直反馈的问题：

> 图漂亮，但是没设计感。

原因：

AI缺少：

```
布局规划
视觉重心
空间关系
比例控制
```

---

需要：

## Layout Intelligence

能力：

```
图片生成前

先生成：

Composition Plan

↓

再生成图片
```

类似：

设计师：

先草图

再制作。

---

开源方向：

## ① LayoutDiffusion

https://github.com/ZGCTroy/LayoutDiffusion


研究：

文本控制布局。

适合：

- 海报
- 电商图
- UI
- 广告

---

## ② GLIGEN

https://github.com/gligen/GLIGEN


非常适合：

控制：

- 物体位置
- 关系
- 空间布局


例如：

```
瓶子
右侧

人物
左侧

文字区域
顶部
```

这比普通 Prompt 强很多。

---

# 3. 排版能力增强

这是商业设计最难的问题之一。

AI图片：

越来越强。

但是：

```
文字
排版
信息层级
```

仍然弱。

---

需要独立：

# Typography Engine


包含：

```
字体选择
字距
行距
层级
网格
比例
留白
```

---

开源参考：

## ① Fabric.js

https://github.com/fabricjs/fabric.js


用于：

画布编辑。


适合：

Open Design Adapter。

---

## ② Paper.js

https://github.com/paperjs/paper.js


适合：

矢量设计逻辑。


---

## ③ Figma Plugin Ecosystem

重点吸收：

不是代码。

而是：

```
Auto Layout
Constraints
Component Logic
Design Tokens
```

---

# 4. 图片生成质量强化

这里不能只靠 SD。

需要：

## Image Generation Pipeline


现在：

```
Prompt
 ↓
图片
```

太简单。

应该：

```
Brief

↓

Reference DNA

↓

Composition

↓

ControlNet

↓

Generation

↓

Critic

↓

Refinement

↓

Upscale

↓

Final
```

---

## 推荐吸收：

---

# ControlNet

https://github.com/lllyasviel/ControlNet


必须吸收。

作用：

控制：

- 构图
- 姿态
- 边缘
- 深度
- 草图

---

# ComfyUI

https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI


非常适合：

作为：

```
Image Pipeline Runtime
```

不是替代 Open Design。

而是：

Open Design 调用后端。

---

# IP-Adapter
